findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a gitlink 'sentry-repo' at the repository root pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, creating a self-referential submodule entry inside the sentry repository itself. Anyone cloning/checking out this branch gets a broken/phantom submodule with no .gitmodules entry; CI and local tooling fail on 'sentry-repo does not have a .gitmodules entry' and the working tree is permanently dirty, blocking merge.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform compares the dataset argument against modules (dataset == errors, dataset == transactions, dataset == discover), but organization_events_stats passes the dataset as a string (e.g. "errors", "discover") from the request's dataset parameter. The string-to-module comparisons are always False, so the function falls through to 'return False' for every real request; upsampling never activates in production and the endpoint tests test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects (expecting count == 10) fail because the plain count() path runs.

[BUG] The upsampled_count SnQLFunction aggregates Column("sample_weight"), a column that does not exist in the Snuba discover/errors dataset schema, and nothing in this diff (or the factory change, which sets 'sample_rate', not 'sample_weight') ever writes a sample_weight value. Any query that reaches this function fails in Snuba with an unknown-column error (500 to the client), and the endpoint test asserting data[0][1][0]['count'] == 10 cannot pass — no machinery computes sample_weight, so even if the column existed the sum would be 0/absent, not 10.

[BUG] The cache key is built with Python's builtin hash() of a tuple of ints, which is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project-id set produces different keys in different workers. Cache entries written by one process are never read by another (and hash() over tuples of ints is randomized across restarts), so the 60-second 'performance optimization' provides near-zero hit rate in multi-process deployments while still paying cache.set on every request.

[BUG] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but no code path anywhere in the diff calls it, so allowlist changes made via options cannot invalidate the 60-second cache as documented. Operators who flip issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist see stale upsampled counts for up to 60s (or longer, per the randomized-hash key issue meaning invalidation can't even target the right key), contradicting the function's stated contract.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling decision is computed once at the top of _get_event_stats but transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns) is invoked separately in three branches (top_events RPC, top_events legacy, timeseries RPC, timeseries legacy = four sites), each re-deriving final_columns. The next change to the transformation (e.g. handling count_unique or equations) must be replicated at four call sites; a missed site silently returns non-upsampled counts for one code path only, a divergence that is invisible until a customer compares widget vs chart numbers.

[ADVISORY] The eligibility result is cached keyed only on organization.id and project_ids, but the cached boolean is then combined with a per-request dataset/request check, and tests in tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py run four mock-patched scenarios sequentially in one process sharing the default cache. The first test caches is_eligible=True for (org, [p1, p2]); the later test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects patches options to [] but may read the stale cached True from the shared locmem cache, producing flaky/order-dependent test failures (and in production, an org that shares project ids across silos gets another org's eligibility only if ids collide — the real hazard is the tests and any future multi-request flows).

[BUG] The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter, but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for the errors dataset, so error-dataset queries emit `upsampled_count()` into a resolver that has no such function. For an allowlisted project querying the errors dataset (the primary case this PR targets), Snuba query building fails with an unknown-function/parse error, returning a 500 from the events-stats endpoint instead of upsampled counts; no test in the diff exercises the errors dataset through the endpoint.

[ADVISORY] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites the exact literal `count()`, silently passing through every other count-family aggregate and equation. A user issuing `yAxis=count_unique(user),count()` or the equation `equation=count()/2` on an allowlisted errors project gets `count_unique`/equation terms computed over sampled rows while `count()` is upsampled — internally inconsistent numbers in one response, with no error or documentation. The tests cover only the exact-match forms, so this mixed-scale response mode is unverified.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but has no caller anywhere in this diff — no options-change hook, API, or signal path invokes it. Operators flipping `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` see stale eligibility for up to 60s per org/project-set key with no way to force invalidation short of waiting or flushing cache; the function is dead code as shipped (ships-inert).

[ADVISORY] The diff sets `sample_rate` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` only in the test factory, and the upsampled_count aggregate sums a `sample_weight` column whose derivation from `sample_rate` appears nowhere in this diff — the 60-second cache and the test assertion `count == 10` both depend on that unstated mapping. The integration tests pass only because test infrastructure fabricates the sampling context; nothing verifies real ingestion writes sample_weight, so production allowlisted projects with events lacking sample_weight will sum to 0 (or null) and the endpoint will silently report zero errors. The helper's docstring 'we rely on the database schema' is an unverified assumption with no test.

[ADVISORY] `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`'s caching behavior (60s TTL, cross-request staleness, cache-hit path short-circuiting the allowlist check) has no test coverage — the test file imports and tests only the private helpers, never this public entry point or the cache path. A regression in cache serialization (e.g., a backend returning the cached boolean as a string, making `cached_result and ...` truthy-but-wrong) or in key construction would ship unverified; also the sibling-flag check `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` is skipped on cache hit for allowlist but re-run per request, an asymmetry nothing exercises.

[ADVISORY] `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check for `event.type:error` in the lowercased query string, missing sibling spellings such as `event.type:exception`, negated `!event.type:transaction` filters, or `error` shorthand that Sentry's search grammar accepts as error-focused. Discover queries that are in fact error-only (e.g. `!event.type:transaction`) return non-upsampled counts on allowlisted projects, producing counts inconsistent with the same query run on the errors dataset — users comparing charts across datasets see divergent numbers with no indication why.

[ADVISORY] The top_events path applies the upsampling transform to y_axes only; the parallel column lists passed on the same path — `get_field_list(organization, request)` selected_columns and `get_orderby(request)` — are never transformed, so a topEvents query with `orderby=count` or `field=count()` mixes raw and upsampled counts. A topEvents request on an allowlisted errors project orders/filters by unweighted count while the timeseries series are upsampled, so the selected 'top' events don't correspond to the series shown next to them; no test in the diff exercises the top_events path with upsampling at all.

[BUG] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' pointing at commit a5d290951de that is not traceable to any part of the stated intent (error upsampling in events stats). Every consumer of this repo gains an unexpected nested repository reference; CI/checkout behavior changes for all users of this PR with no requirement justifying it, and the commit content is unauditable from this diff.

[BUG] The cache key is built with Python's built-in hash(), which is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so cache.get(cache_key) and cache.set(cache_key, ...) compute different keys in different web workers and even across restarts of the same worker. The 60-second 'performance optimization' cache never hits across processes: every request recomputes the allowlist check (perf claim false) and invalidate_upsampling_cache (line 71) deletes a key no worker ever reads, so config changes never propagate via the advertised invalidation path.

[BUG] The eligibility cache stores only the allowlist decision keyed by org+projects but the caller passes different datasets/requests through the same key path, and more importantly the cached decision is checked after computing it without the dataset gate on the cache-miss branch ordering — but the real under-enforced invariant is that the SnQLFunction 'upsampled_count' (discover.py:1041-1053) is registered publicly (no private=True) with no allowlist check at the query layer. Any authenticated user in any organization can write yAxis=upsampled_count() directly against the org events stats endpoint and get sum(sample_weight) results for non-allowlisted projects, silently bypassing the 'all projects must be allowlisted' invariant the helper module is supposed to enforce; upsampling leaks as a generally available aggregate.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling and calls it unconditionally from store_event (line 1048), modifying shared test infrastructure used by every existing event-storing test, not just the new upsampling tests. Every test that stores events with an error_sampling context silently gains a sample_rate; the behavior change is untraceable to the endpoint requirement and any future test asserting sample_rate behavior or normalization output will see altered data with no gating on the allowlist or the new tests.

[ADVISORY] The error message text is changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1', which is unrelated to error upsampling. Unrelated drift in a public API error payload; any client or test asserting the old message string breaks, and the change has no requirement behind it.

[ADVISORY] The diff seeds upsampling_enabled/final_columns and then repeats the identical 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block three times (top_events, RPC, and standard paths), duplicating a decision already computed once at the top. The next change to the transformation (e.g., handling other aggregates) requires editing three sites; the triple-branch already drifted from the single-decision comment above it, and deleting the repetition would remove ~9 lines and two places-to-update.

[ADVISORY] The cached eligibility result is computed and cached before the dataset gate is applied, and the cache-miss path never re-checks the cache within the same request flow, but the substantive gap is that _are_all_projects_error_upsampled's allowlist option is read directly while is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled caches for 60s with no caller anywhere in this diff invoking invalidate_upsampling_cache. invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code in this diff — no option-change hook, signal receiver, or admin path calls it — so when an operator removes a project from the allowlist, up to 60 seconds of queries continue returning upsampled counts for a now-ineligible project; the ship includes an invalidation API nobody wires up.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's builtin hash() on a tuple of project ids, which is not stable across processes under hash randomization, so every worker process computes a different key for the same (org, projects) pair. The cache never hits across workers, making the 60s 'performance optimization' a pure cache.set with no reuse in multi-process deployments, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() computed in whichever process handles the config change deletes a key no other worker will ever read — stale eligibility persists up to 60s and the invalidation is a silent no-op.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to upsampled_count() which sums a 'sample_weight' column, but nothing in this diff ever writes sample_weight — the test factory helper _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling sets a 'sample_rate' field on normalized event data, not 'sample_weight', and no ingestion path in the diff populates the column. For real deployments the sum(sample_weight) aggregate sums a column that is null/absent for all events, so upsampled counts return 0 (or the query fails outright if the column doesn't exist in the Snuba schema), silently replacing correct count() values with garbage on every stats request for allowlisted projects — a sentinel-meaning-change where the yAxis 'count()' result silently becomes 0.

[BUG] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling mutates normalized_data for every store_event call in the entire test suite, not just upsampling tests, applying a blanket try/except-swallowed transform to all event factories globally. Any existing test whose event payload happens to carry an error_sampling context now gets a sample_rate injected, changing normalization behavior suite-wide; the bare except Exception also silently swallows non-dict contexts values (e.g. contexts being a list), masking data-shape regressions instead of surfacing them.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in this diff, so the advertised cache-consistency mechanism is dead code and allowlist option changes propagate only via 60s TTL expiry. Operators flipping issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist see mixed upsampled/raw counts for up to a minute across workers with no way to force consistency; the function's docstring promises invalidation behavior the system never performs.

[ADVISORY] Only the exact string 'count()' (case/whitespace-insensitive) is transformed, so aliased or nested count aggregations like 'count() as total', 'count(unique(user))', or equation-based counts pass through untransformed while plain count() is upsampled in the same response. A single stats request with yAxis='count(),count_unique(user)' returns an upsampled count next to a raw unique count — mixed sampling semantics in one payload that misleads any dashboard comparing the two series; users hitting the API with 'count() as total' get silently non-upsampled numbers.

[ADVISORY] For the discover dataset, eligibility is decided by substring-matching 'event.type:error' in the raw lowercased query string, which misses every semantically-equivalent error query form (no event.type filter, 'event.type:error OR ...' composed with free-text, issue-stream queries where the type is implied). Discover queries that return only errors but omit the literal token bypass upsampling and show sampled (10x-undercounted) counts, while an adjacent query with event.type:error shows upsampled counts for the same projects — inconsistent numbers within the same dashboard depending on query phrasing.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's upsampling decision is made by calling is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects on every stats request, and on cache miss it performs an options.get plus per-project allowlist membership scans with no guard on the number of project_ids, all before any cheap early-exit on malformed params. Org-wide queries with hundreds of projects do an O(n) scan against a list-typed allowlist (list membership, not a set) on every uncached request; converting the allowlist to a set is a one-line fix, but as written the hot stats path pays a linear scan per request plus a cache round-trip keyed by an unstable hash (see related finding).

[ADVISORY] The transformation block is duplicated three times (top_events path, RPC path, standard path), each re-deriving final_columns from query_columns with its own 'if upsampling_enabled' guard, instead of transforming once where upsampling_enabled is computed. A fourth query path or a change to the transformation (e.g. also rewriting count_unique) must be applied in three places; the drift risk is concrete — one path already omits the transform-visible handling for referrer/config differences, and the next editor adding a path will copy the wrong variant. The single transformation final_columns = transform(...) after line 222 makes all three guards deletions.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash() on a tuple of project ids, which is randomized per process, so the same project set produces different keys in different workers and cache.get always misses (or hits unrelated processes' stale keys). The advertised 60s performance cache never actually works cross-process, and worse, invalidate_upsampling_cache() constructs a key with a different per-process hash than the one that wrote it, so allowlist changes are never invalidated anywhere — an allowlisted-later project keeps non-upsampled (undercounted) error numbers for the cache TTL and vice versa.

[ADVISORY] The PR title promises 'upsampled error count'; review iterations silently added an unreviewed 60-second eventual-consistency window on the allowlist decision, changing the correctness contract of the counts API without any human sign-off documented in the diff. Operators toggling issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist see mixed old/new count() semantics for up to 60 seconds; a dashboard requested twice in that window shows two different error counts for the same time range, with no way to disable the cache (no option, no feature flag).

[ADVISORY] The docstring on _are_all_projects_error_upsampled says 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... to ensure we always have the latest configuration state', which is directly falsified by the caching wrapper that calls it — the intent documented in the code and the actual behavior are contradictory after the review-driven caching change. The next maintainer trusting the docstring will reason about fresh-read semantics that no longer exist (up to 60s staleness), and the doc-vs-code drift makes the caching change look intentional/accepted when it was a silent objective change.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies the global store_event factory to inject a sample_rate from contexts.error_sampling into every stored event across the entire test suite, a test-infrastructure-wide behavioral change smuggled in to make the upsampling endpoint tests pass rather than implementing the production write path for sample_weight. Any unrelated existing test that stores events carrying an error_sampling context now gets a sample_rate it did not have before, silently changing outcomes in tests outside this feature; meanwhile production still has no code writing the sample_weight column the whole design depends on, so the shipped upsampling only works against test-injected data.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently rewrites an unrelated user-facing error message ('If topEvents needs to be at least 1' -> 'topEvents needs to be at least 1') with no connection to error upsampling, a drive-by change that was never part of the stated feature intent. Clients (including Sentry's own frontend tests and any external API consumer asserting on the response detail string) see a changed error message on a validation path untouched by the feature, breaking assumptions with no migration note or acceptance.

[ADVISORY] _is_error_focused_query was 'reduced to only check for event.type:error' per its own comment, silently narrowing the original intent: any discover-dataset error query that doesn't literally contain the string 'event.type:error' (e.g. 'message:boom', 'level:error', queries built by dashboards that rely on dataset defaults) is excluded from upsampling. Users on allowlisted projects get inconsistently upsampled counts depending on how they phrased the query — a discover query filtered by level:error shows undercounted true counts while event.type:error shows upsampled counts in the same dashboard, producing silently mismatched numbers with no indication of which semantics apply.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' pointing at an unreviewed external commit a5d290951de alongside the feature change, shipping unknown third-party code into the repository. Anyone (or any CI pipeline) cloning with --recurse-submodules pulls and builds code that went through no review; if the submodule contains build hooks or vendored source that ends up imported, the attacker-controlled commit executes in the trusted build — operators bitten at the next full clone/CI run.

[ADVISORY] The eligibility decision is cached for 60 seconds keyed only on (org, project_ids), and invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, so allowlist removals are served stale with no operator path to force invalidation. An admin who removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees inflated (sum-of-sample_weight) error counts continue to be served for up to 60 seconds per cache entry, with no way to flush it short of waiting out the TTL — and since the same key is written per distinct project-id combination, entries regenerate on every query.

[BUG] The four upsampling endpoint tests share the module-level 'error_upsampling_eligible' cache with no cache reset in setUp/tearDown, so results depend on alphabetical test-execution order. test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects caches True for the (org, project_ids) key; test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects and test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist then hit that stale entry, take the upsampled path despite the mocked empty/partial allowlist, and their `assert data[0][1][0]['count'] == 1` assertions fail (they get 10), or the tests silently stop verifying the allowlist logic entirely if ordering changes again — either way the non-allowlisted paths are never actually verified.

[BUG] The only public entry point, is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, including its cache-hit branch and invalidate_upsampling_cache, has zero test coverage in the new test file (checked tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py, which imports only _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling). The cache-hit path `if cached_result is not None: return cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` is never executed by any test, and invalidate_upsampling_cache (a public API the PR adds for config-change consistency) is never called anywhere in the diff — a regression in cache serialization (e.g. cache.get returning a non-bool) or in invalidation would pass the entire suite, and the 'performance optimization' claim in the PR title is tested for no behavior at all.

[ADVISORY] test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects asserts data[0][1][0]['count'] == 10, but nothing in this diff implements the sample_weight ingestion that would produce 10 — the only ingest-side change is _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling setting 'sample_rate' on normalized data in factories.py, and the actual sample_weight column population lives in the opaque sentry-repo submodule commit. If the ingestion pipeline does not derive sample_weight from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate, sum(sample_weight) returns 0 or errors and this test fails; if it does, the test's correctness hinges on an unstated cross-repo dependency with no assertion that sample_weight itself was set (no test inspects the stored event's sample_weight value), so a regression in that derivation is only caught indirectly and confusingly as an endpoint count mismatch.

[ADVISORY] test_are_all_projects_error_upsampled mocks the entire options module, so the real options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', []) call — including its default-value argument — is never exercised. If the option key is renamed or the default [] is dropped in the helper (making options.get raise on a nonexistent key with no default), the test still passes because the Mock returns whatever return_value is set; the mismatch between the tested option key and the production option key (e.g. a typo in the string) is invisible to this suite.

[ADVISORY] The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction registration (its toInt64/sum(sample_weight) aggregate and its default_result_type='number', which differs from count()'s 'integer') has no direct test asserting the function resolves, its output type, or its SQL shape — the endpoint tests exercise it only through the full API happy path with a mocked allowlist. A typo in the function name, a wrong alias, or the number-vs-integer result-type inconsistency would surface only as a confusing downstream API failure in integration tests (or not at all if the number type coerces silently), and consumers doing integer-typed arithmetic on the response get a silent type change with no test pinning the contract.

[BUG] The upsampling transform replaces count() with sum(sample_weight) for allowlisted projects, but no migration, backfill, or writer anywhere in this diff populates sample_weight for existing or incoming error events in the Snuba errors dataset. Events stored before this change (and events from SDKs that don't send contexts.error_sampling) have no sample_weight, so sum(sample_weight) returns NULL/0 instead of the event count — dashboards for allowlisted projects silently show zero counts, i.e. the migration from count() to sample_weight has no backfill step and the cutover loses data on day one.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling is applied to ALL count() aggregates across all queried projects once eligibility is cached True, with no per-event guard that sample_weight exists. For any event lacking sample_weight (historical rows in allowlisted projects during the transition window), the aggregation silently drops those rows from the count — the classic read-new-column-before-backfill dual-write gap; the comment 'we rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists' is an unexamined assumption contradicted by this diff, which contains no schema change at all.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query detects error queries via a raw substring match on "event.type:error" in request.GET['query'], so any query containing that substring anywhere (e.g. a search for a literal token like `message:"event.type:error"` or a negated `!event.type:error`) is misclassified. A discover query mixing transactions with a literal/negated event.type:error token gets count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight); transactions have no sample_weight, so the returned counts are NULL/0 — silent wrong numbers for mixed queries during and after rollout.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash() on the sorted project-id tuple, which is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED) while the Sentry cache is a shared backend. Different region-silo workers compute different keys for the same project set, so invalidate_upsampling_cache called from the process that changes the allowlist deletes a key no other worker ever reads — the 60s stale-eligibility cache cannot be invalidated across processes, meaning queries keep returning upsampled (sample_weight-based, NULL-summing) counts for up to 60s after a project is removed from the allowlist during an incident rollback.

[ADVISORY] The only code path in this diff that derives a sample rate from contexts.error_sampling is the test factory's _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, with no corresponding production event-ingestion writer. The feature ships with a reader (upsampled_count summing sample_weight) but no production writer for sample_weight — an expand-phase read with no expand-phase write, so the endpoint's behavior in production is unrepresentable except through this test-only shim; whoever adds the real writer later must also add the backfill this diff is missing.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache takes a project_ids sequence and deletes only the exact combined-tuple key, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches per (org, exact project-set-tuple), so a query spanning a different subset of projects (e.g. [1,2] vs [1,2,3]) has separate cache entries that invalidation never touches. An operator removing project 3 from the allowlist and invalidating [1,2,3] still leaves the cached True for [1,3] queries, which then sums a sample_weight column project 3's events don't have — stale-cache-driven data loss that the invalidation API cannot reach.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query does a raw substring match on "event.type:error", so a negated query like "!event.type:error" or "NOT event.type:error" is classified as error-focused and gets the sample_weight transform applied. On the discover dataset, a query explicitly excluding errors (e.g. `query=!event.type:error`) has count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over transaction rows, where sample_weight does not exist — the Snuba query fails or returns 0/garbage counts for a query the user explicitly scoped to non-error events.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only the literal token "count()"; every other aggregation in the same request (count_unique(...), count_if(...), percentile(...), and equations referencing count) is passed through unchanged, so a single response mixes upsampled and raw counts with no log, error, or warning. Users on allowlisted projects querying yAxis=count(),count_unique(user) get one axis scaled by 1/sample_weight and the other on raw event counts in the same chart — silently inconsistent data that looks valid and is hard to debug; equations over count() also use the raw value while the displayed count is upsampled.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, so allowlist changes are never propagated and stale eligibility is served for up to 60 seconds. An operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees inflated upsampled counts continue for up to a minute after the change, with no way to force invalidation short of waiting out the TTL or flushing the shared cache; the invalidation hook is dead code.

[ADVISORY] The eligibility cache key is built with Python's built-in hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), and cache.set is executed unconditionally on the request path — including for orgs whose projects are not allowlisted and for transaction/span queries that can never use upsampling. Every stats request for any organization performs a shared-cache write (including a False value for every non-eligible org), adding a distributed cache round-trip write to a high-traffic endpoint; and the hash-based key means invalidate_upsampling_cache only matches if the caller passes the exact same project-id set, so partial-set invalidation silently no-ops for any different combination of projects.

[ADVISORY] The cached eligibility result is returned without re-checking the allowlist, but on cache miss the eligibility AND the dataset check are evaluated — meaning the cache stores an org/project-set decision that is only valid for the allowlist state at write time while a concurrent allowlist update between two requests yields different answers with no consistency mechanism beyond the 60s TTL. During allowlist rollouts, two identical requests seconds apart return different count scales (one raw, one upsampled) with no way to tell from the response which was applied, producing visible count jumps in dashboards; the inline comments claim 'ensures consistent behavior' which misrepresents the actual semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key is built with Python's builtin hash() of a tuple of ints, which is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project-id set produces different keys in different workers. Cache entries written by one process are never read by another (and hash() over tuples of ints is randomized across restarts), so the 60-second 'performance optimization' provides near-zero hit rate in multi-process deployments while still paying cache.set on every request.

[BUG] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but no code path anywhere in the diff calls it, so allowlist changes made via options cannot invalidate the 60-second cache as documented. adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is newly defined in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` but there is no call site added here, so the documented “should be called when the allowlist configuration changes” hook is not actually wired up by this PR. Also, the cache key uses Python’s built-in `hash(tuple(...))`, which is process-randomized, so any future cross-process invalidation (and even shared-cache hit rate) would be unreliable. However, the claim that this “contradicts” behavior is overstated: the upsampling check explicitly documents 60s eventual consistency (`cache.set(..., 60)`), so stale results up to the TTL are intentional, and the diff does not show staleness lasting longer than 60s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key uses Python's builtin hash() on a tuple of project ids, which is not stable across processes under hash randomization, so every worker process computes a different key for the same (org, projects) pair. adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is newly introduced and its docstring describes it as something that “should be called when the allowlist configuration changes,” but there is no caller added anywhere in this diff (only the caching read/write is used in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`). As a result, allowlist changes can only take effect via the hardcoded 60s TTL in `cache.set(..., 60)`, and the invalidation mechanism is currently unused/dead code in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Only the exact string 'count()' (case/whitespace-insensitive) is transformed, so aliased or nested count aggregations like 'count() as total', 'count(unique(user))', or equation-based counts pass through untransformed while plain count() is upsampled in the same response. A single stats request with yAxis='count(),count_unique(user)' returns an upsampled count next to a raw unique count — mixed sampling semantics in one payload that misleads any dashboard comparing the two series; users hitting the API with 'count() as total' get silently non-upsampled numbers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` only rewrites columns whose lowercased/stripped form is exactly `"count()"` (see `if column_lower == "count()": ...`). Any aliased/extended forms like `"count() as total"` or other count-like aggregations will not be transformed, while a plain `count()` in the same request will be. This can lead to mixed semantics across multiple `yAxis` values in one response (some series upsampled, others not) and silently missing upsampling when users alias `count()`. The behavior is consistent with the diff, but it’s an incomplete/edge-case handling concern rather than a definite broken behavior proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] For the discover dataset, eligibility is decided by substring-matching 'event.type:error' in the raw lowercased query string, which misses every semantically-equivalent error query form (no event.type filter, 'event.type:error OR ...' composed with free-text, issue-stream queries where the type is implied). Discover queries that return only errors but omit the literal token bypass upsampling and show sampled (10x-undercounted) counts, while an adjacent query with event.type:error shows upsampled counts for the same projects — inconsistent numbers within the same dashboard depending on query phrasing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly implements discover-dataset eligibility via a raw substring check: `_is_error_focused_query` lowercases `request.GET.get("query", "")` and returns True only if it contains the literal token `"event.type:error"` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py). `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` uses this for `dataset == discover`, so semantically error-only discover queries that don’t include that exact token will not be upsampled. The diff even documents this limitation (“Reduced to only check for event.type:error to err on the side of caution.”). Whether this is a “defect” depends on intended semantics, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/inconsistency concern rather than a misread.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint's upsampling decision is made by calling is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects on every stats request, and on cache miss it performs an options.get plus per-project allowlist membership scans with no guard on the number of project_ids, all before any cheap early-exit on malformed params. Org-wide queries with hundreds of projects do an O(n) scan against a list-typed allowlist (list membership, not a set) on every uncached request; converting the allowlist to a set is a one-line fix, but as written the hot stats path pays a linear scan per request plus a cache round-trip keyed by an unstable hash (see related finding).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` in `organization_events_stats.py` and calls it for every stats request inside `_get_event_stats`. On a cache miss, `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` does `allowlist = options.get(..., [])` and then `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`, where `allowlist` is a list and `in` is linear, yielding an avoidable O(n) (or worse) scan for large `project_ids`. There is no guard/short-circuit based on project count, and the work happens before query execution. This is a concrete hot-path performance concern introduced by the new helper, but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The transformation block is duplicated three times (top_events path, RPC path, standard path), each re-deriving final_columns from query_columns with its own 'if upsampling_enabled' guard, instead of transforming once where upsampling_enabled is computed. A fourth query path or a change to the transformation (e.g. also rewriting count_unique) must be applied in three places; the drift risk is concrete — one path already omits the transform-visible handling for referrer/config differences, and the next editor adding a path will copy the wrong variant. The single transformation final_columns = transform(...) after line 222 makes all three guards deletions.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats.py` `_get_event_stats`, `final_columns` is derived from `query_columns` and then conditionally transformed under `if upsampling_enabled` in three separate places: (1) inside the `if top_events > 0` block, (2) inside the `if use_rpc` (non-top-events) block, and (3) again just before the non-RPC `timeseries_query` call. This duplication is visible in the diff and creates real maintenance/drift risk if the transformation logic expands (e.g., beyond `count()`) or another query path is added, even though it is not a current correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash() on a tuple of project ids, which is randomized per process, so the same project set produces different keys in different workers and cache.get always misses (or hits unrelated processes' stale keys). The advertised 60s performance cache never actually works cross-process, and worse, invalidate_upsampling_cache() constructs a key with a different per-process hash than the one that wrote it, so allowlist changes are never invalidated anywhere — an allowlisted-later project keeps non-upsampled (undercounted) error numbers for the cache TTL and vice versa.

adjudication.rationale: In `sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, the cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Python’s built-in `hash()` is not stable across processes (hash randomization), so different workers will compute different keys for the same project-id set in a shared cache. That makes the cached eligibility effectively per-process (reducing intended cache effectiveness) and also means `invalidate_upsampling_cache()` (which uses the same `hash(...)` expression) cannot reliably delete keys written by other processes, so cache invalidation on allowlist changes is broken across workers.

Operators toggling issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist see mixed old/new count() semantics for up to 60 seconds; a dashboard requested twice in that window shows two different error counts for the same time range, with no way to disable the cache (no option, no feature flag).

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a cached allowlist-eligibility decision in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` using `cache.set(..., 60)` (new file `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`). This means changes to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` may not affect query behavior for up to 60 seconds, causing temporary inconsistency in whether `count()` is transformed to `upsampled_count()` (via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` in `organization_events_stats.py`). That is a real, diff-grounded behavior/contract concern (hardcoded TTL, no flag/option to disable), but it’s not a clear correctness “bug” since the code documents it as an intentional performance optimization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The docstring on _are_all_projects_error_upsampled says 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... to ensure we always have the latest configuration state', which is directly falsified by the caching wrapper that calls it — the intent documented in the code and the actual behavior are contradictory after the review-driven caching change. The next maintainer trusting the docstring will reason about fresh-read semantics that no longer exist (up to 60s staleness), and the doc-vs-code drift makes the caching change look intentional/accepted when it was a silent objective change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The eligibility decision is cached for 60 seconds keyed only on (org, project_ids), and invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, so allowlist removals are served stale with no operator path to force invalidation. An admin who removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees inflated (sum-of-sample_weight) error counts continue to be served for up to 60 seconds per cache entry, with no way to flush it short of waiting out the TTL — and since the same key is written per distinct project-id combination, entries regenerate on every query.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a 60s cache in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` keyed as `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(sorted(project_ids))}` and writes `cache.set(..., 60)` on miss. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The four upsampling endpoint tests share the module-level 'error_upsampling_eligible' cache with no cache reset in setUp/tearDown, so results depend on alphabetical test-execution order. test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects caches True for the (org, project_ids) key; test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects and test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist then hit that stale entry, take the upsampled path despite the mocked empty/partial allowlist, and their `assert data[0][1][0]['count'] == 1` assertions fail (they get 10), or the tests silently stop verifying the allowlist logic entirely if ordering changes again — either way the non-allowlisted paths are never actually verified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a real cross-test contamination risk: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` now caches allowlist eligibility in the global `cache` for 60s under a key derived from `(organization.id, sorted(project_ids))` (see `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`). The four endpoint tests in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` each patch `options.get` to different allowlist values, but they do not clear/invalidate this cache in `setUp`/`tearDown`. If the same org + project_ids are used across those tests (which is what the test code suggests, since both projects are queried together each time), the first test that populates the cache can force subsequent tests down the cached path regardless of their mocked allowlist, making results depend on execution order and potentially causing the asserted non-allowlisted counts (==1) to incorrectly become upsampled (==10).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only public entry point, is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, including its cache-hit branch and invalidate_upsampling_cache, has zero test coverage in the new test file (checked tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py, which imports only _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects asserts data[0][1][0]['count'] == 10, but nothing in this diff implements the sample_weight ingestion that would produce 10 — the only ingest-side change is _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling setting 'sample_rate' on normalized data in factories.py, and the actual sample_weight column population lives in the opaque sentry-repo submodule commit. The new API test `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` expects `count == 10` from events stored with `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate = 0.1`, but in this diff the only ingest-side change is `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` setting `normalized_data['sample_rate']`; there is no visible code here that derives/persists `sample_weight` from that value. Since the PR also adds an opaque `sentry-repo` submodule commit, the test’s correctness depends on cross-repo/hidden ingestion behavior and does not directly assert `sample_weight` was set, making failures potentially indirect and confusing. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The upsampling transform replaces count() with sum(sample_weight) for allowlisted projects, but no migration, backfill, or writer anywhere in this diff populates sample_weight for existing or incoming error events in the Snuba errors dataset. Events stored before this change (and events from SDKs that don't send contexts.error_sampling) have no sample_weight, so sum(sample_weight) returns NULL/0 instead of the event count — dashboards for allowlisted projects silently show zero counts, i.e. the migration from count() to sample_weight has no backfill step and the cutover loses data on day one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a transformation from `count()` to `upsampled_count()` (which is implemented as `sum(sample_weight)`) via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, and the new SnQL function in `discover.py` sums `sample_weight` without any `coalesce`/defaulting. However, whether `sample_weight` is populated (historically or on ingest) is not verifiable from this PR alone: there is no schema/migration or ingest writer code shown here, and the PR even adds test-only plumbing to set `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`, implying the broader pipeline may already derive `sample_weight` elsewhere. So the finding is a legitimate diff-grounded risk/assumption gap (needs confirmation/backfill guarantees), but not a provable defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling is applied to ALL count() aggregates across all queried projects once eligibility is cached True, with no per-event guard that sample_weight exists. For any event lacking sample_weight (historical rows in allowlisted projects during the transition window), the aggregation silently drops those rows from the count — the classic read-new-column-before-backfill dual-write gap; the comment 'we rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists' is an unexamined assumption contradicted by this diff, which contains no schema change at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does hard-switch `count()` to `upsampled_count()` (implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`) whenever `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` returns true, and there is no fallback/guard if `sample_weight` is missing or unset for some rows (see `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` and the new `upsampled_count` in `discover.py`). The PR also contains no schema/backfill/dual-write coordination to substantiate the comment that `sample_weight` “exists for all events”, so correctness during rollout is a legitimate concern. However, the finding overstates one point: the cached eligibility is keyed by org + the specific `project_ids` set, so it’s not applied to “ALL queried projects” globally once any cache entry is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query detects error queries via a raw substring match on "event.type:error" in request.GET['query'], so any query containing that substring anywhere (e.g. a search for a literal token like `message:"event.type:error"` or a negated `!event.type:error`) is misclassified. A discover query mixing transactions with a literal/negated event.type:error token gets count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight); transactions have no sample_weight, so the returned counts are NULL/0 — silent wrong numbers for mixed queries during and after rollout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `_is_error_focused_query` which lowercases `request.GET['query']` and returns True on a raw substring check: `if "event.type:error" in query:`. This will also match negated tokens like `!event.type:error` and occurrences inside quoted literals (e.g. `message:"event.type:error"`), causing `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` to return True for the `discover` dataset when the query is not actually error-focused. That in turn enables `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` to rewrite `count()` to `upsampled_count()` in `organization_events_stats.py`, potentially applying `sum(sample_weight)` where it shouldn’t.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash() on the sorted project-id tuple, which is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED) while the Sentry cache is a shared backend. Different region-silo workers compute different keys for the same project set, so invalidate_upsampling_cache called from the process that changes the allowlist deletes a key no other worker ever reads — the 60s stale-eligibility cache cannot be invalidated across processes, meaning queries keep returning upsampled (sample_weight-based, NULL-summing) counts for up to 60s after a project is removed from the allowlist during an incident rollback.

adjudication.rationale: In `sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, the cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"` (and the same pattern is used in `invalidate_upsampling_cache`). Python’s built-in `hash()` is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different worker processes can compute different keys for the same project-id set when using a shared cache backend. That makes cross-process cache invalidation unreliable (deleting a different key than other workers used), and also prevents cache sharing across workers, leaving stale eligibility decisions to persist until TTL expiry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only code path in this diff that derives a sample rate from contexts.error_sampling is the test factory's _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, with no corresponding production event-ingestion writer. The feature ships with a reader (upsampled_count summing sample_weight) but no production writer for sample_weight — an expand-phase read with no expand-phase write, so the endpoint's behavior in production is unrepresentable except through this test-only shim; whoever adds the real writer later must also add the backfill this diff is missing.

The only place in this diff that derives any sampling-related value from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is a test utility change (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` in `testutils/factories.py`), and there is no corresponding production ingestion/write-path change shown here to ensure `sample_weight` is present/populated. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded completeness/architecture concern, though the claim that production has no writer/backfill cannot be fully verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache takes a project_ids sequence and deletes only the exact combined-tuple key, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches per (org, exact project-set-tuple), so a query spanning a different subset of projects (e.g. [1,2] vs [1,2,3]) has separate cache entries that invalidation never touches. An operator removing project 3 from the allowlist and invalidating [1,2,3] still leaves the cached True for [1,3] queries, which then sums a sample_weight column project 3's events don't have — stale-cache-driven data loss that the invalidation API cannot reach.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches eligibility under a key that includes `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, i.e., one cache entry per exact project-id set. `invalidate_upsampling_cache(organization_id, project_ids)` deletes only the single key for the exact provided `project_ids`, so it cannot invalidate other cached combinations (e.g. `[1,3]` vs `[1,2,3]`). That makes the invalidation helper incomplete/limited relative to how caching is done. However, the diff does not show this invalidation function being used anywhere, and the cache TTL is only 60s, so the concrete operational “data loss” scenario depends on external usage/assumptions not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query does a raw substring match on "event.type:error", so a negated query like "!event.type:error" or "NOT event.type:error" is classified as error-focused and gets the sample_weight transform applied. On the discover dataset, a query explicitly excluding errors (e.g. `query=!event.type:error`) has count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over transaction rows, where sample_weight does not exist — the Snuba query fails or returns 0/garbage counts for a query the user explicitly scoped to non-error events.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` returns True based on a raw substring check: `if "event.type:error" in query:`. This will incorrectly classify negated/excluding queries like `!event.type:error` or `NOT event.type:error` as “error-focused”. For the `discover` dataset, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` uses `_is_error_focused_query(request)` to decide whether to apply the transformation, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()`, which in `discover.py` is implemented as `sum(sample_weight)`. The helper explicitly notes `sample_weight` “doesn't exist for transactions”, so applying this to a discover query that excludes errors can lead to invalid/garbage results or query failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only the literal token "count()"; every other aggregation in the same request (count_unique(...), count_if(...), percentile(...), and equations referencing count) is passed through unchanged, so a single response mixes upsampled and raw counts with no log, error, or warning. Users on allowlisted projects querying yAxis=count(),count_unique(user) get one axis scaled by 1/sample_weight and the other on raw event counts in the same chart — silently inconsistent data that looks valid and is hard to debug; equations over count() also use the raw value while the displayed count is upsampled.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` only rewrites the exact normalized string `"count()"` into `"upsampled_count() as count"` and leaves all other aggregations unchanged (e.g., `count_unique(...)`, `count_if(...)`, percentiles). In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, only `query_columns`/`y_axes`/`selected_columns` are conditionally transformed; `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` is passed through untouched. This means a request with multiple yAxes can indeed mix one upsampled series (count) with other raw aggregations in the same response without any explicit indication, which is a diff-grounded behavioral concern. However, the diff does not establish that other aggregations should or even can be upsampled correctly (e.g., uniques generally cannot be recovered by simple weighting), and the claim about equations definitively using “raw count” is not verifiable from this diff alone since equation semantics are outside the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, so allowlist changes are never propagated and stale eligibility is served for up to 60 seconds. An operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees inflated upsampled counts continue for up to a minute after the change, with no way to force invalidation short of waiting out the TTL or flushing the shared cache; the invalidation hook is dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In the new helper `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is introduced (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py) but there is no usage shown anywhere in this diff; eligibility is instead cached via `cache.set(..., 60)` in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. That means allowlist changes won’t take effect until cache expiry (up to 60s) unless some external caller (not shown) invokes invalidation. This is a real operational/architecture concern and potentially dead code, but it’s not a strict correctness bug since the code explicitly opts into short-lived staleness via TTL and still eventually converges.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The eligibility cache key is built with Python's built-in hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), and cache.set is executed unconditionally on the request path — including for orgs whose projects are not allowlisted and for transaction/span queries that can never use upsampling. Every stats request for any organization performs a shared-cache write (including a False value for every non-eligible org), adding a distributed cache round-trip write to a high-traffic endpoint; and the hash-based key means invalidate_upsampling_cache only matches if the caller passes the exact same project-id set, so partial-set invalidation silently no-ops for any different combination of projects.

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` the cache key uses Python’s built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python’s `hash()` is process-salted by default, so the same `project_ids` set will produce different keys across different workers/processes, causing distributed-cache misses and making `invalidate_upsampling_cache()` unreliable when called from a different process (it computes a different key). The diff also shows `cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)` happens on every cache miss even when `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` will later make the overall result False (e.g., transactions), which is a performance concern, but the hash-based key is a verifiable correctness defect for a shared cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cached eligibility result is returned without re-checking the allowlist, but on cache miss the eligibility AND the dataset check are evaluated — meaning the cache stores an org/project-set decision that is only valid for the allowlist state at write time while a concurrent allowlist update between two requests yields different answers with no consistency mechanism beyond the 60s TTL. During allowlist rollouts, two identical requests seconds apart return different count scales (one raw, one upsampled) with no way to tell from the response which was applied, producing visible count jumps in dashboards; the inline comments claim 'ensures consistent behavior' which misrepresents the actual semantics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces caching of allowlist eligibility for 60s in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects()` via `cache.get/set` keyed by org + project set, and on cache hit it does not re-check the allowlist (`cached_result` is used directly). This means allowlist changes can yield different upsampling behavior across requests within the TTL window, which can change returned `count()` scaling (raw vs `upsampled_count()`) with no explicit signal in the response. However this is described as an acceptable eventual-consistency tradeoff in the helper docstring (“eventual consistency is acceptable”), so it’s more a rollout/consistency semantics concern and comment accuracy issue than a verifiable correctness bug in the code as written.
